title: Reconstructed finite-point Hom comparison with arbitrary target
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R$, a uniformizer $\varpi$, and $n\ge1$. Put $A=R/\varpi^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $B=A_s$ on the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf].
For an $A$-module $M$ set $L(M)=B\otimes_{\underline A}\underline M=\underline M$, with sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and write $\Gamma=\Gamma(s,-)$. Both functors are exact, $\Gamma B=A$ through $a\mapsto a\cdot1$, and $L\dashv\Gamma$ has the adjunction formulas $h\mapsto(m\mapsto h_s(1\otimes m))$ and $t\mapsto(b\otimes m\mapsto b\,t(m)|_U)$. Apply these functors termwise on complexes and then on derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For every $C\in D^b_c(s,A)$ [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility], the complex $c=\Gamma C$ has bounded finite cohomology [def-weil-point-finite-cohomology-complexes], the actual counit $e_C:Lc\to C$ is an isomorphism, and the unit $u_c:c\to\Gamma Lc$ satisfies $\Gamma(e_C)u_c=1_c$.
For every ambient $V\in D(s_{\mathrm{proet}},B)$ use derived internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. For a flat-term K-flat representative $P$ of $c$ [def-pc-kflat-complex] and a K-injective resolution $V\to J$ [def-pur-kinjective-complex], $\Gamma J$ is K-injective, $\Gamma V\to\Gamma J$ is a quasi-isomorphism, and the chain isomorphism
$$q_{P,J}:\Gamma\mathcal Hom_B^\bullet(LP,J)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_A^\bullet(P,\Gamma J),\qquad h\mapsto(x\mapsto h(1\otimes x))$$
uses differential $dh=d_Jh-(-1)^{\deg h}hd_P$ on both sides [def-pur-hom-complex]. It gives an isomorphism $q_{c,V}:\Gamma R\mathcal Hom_B(Lc,V)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\operatorname{Hom}_A(c,\Gamma V)$. The composite
$$Q_{C,V}=q_{c,V}\circ\Gamma R\mathcal Hom_B(e_C,V):\Gamma R\mathcal Hom_B(C,V)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\operatorname{Hom}_A(c,\Gamma V)$$
is independent of the resolving representatives and is natural, contravariantly in $C$ and covariantly in $V$, for all derived morphisms.

proof.text: For the ordinary signed evaluation used by the model map, apply the proved module_hom_signed_evaluation to the arbitrary unbounded complexes P and J. This supplies existence with exactly the prescribed values on pure tensors. Two such chain maps agree degreewise: the total tensor coproduct extensionality reduces to every (p,j) summand, and tensor-product extensionality reduces to x tensor h, where the two normalization equations agree. This proves ordinaryEvaluation_existsUnique without any remaining hole. The following eight steps remain the plan for the still-unproved finite_point_reconstructed_hom_model.

source.place: Tags 0A8H and 0A8X: signed ordinary evaluation; uniqueness by tensor and coproduct universal properties.

proof.text: Since $B=\underline A$, multiplication $b\otimes m\mapsto bm$, with inverse $m\mapsto1\otimes m$, identifies $L(M)$ with $\underline M$. Constant presheaves preserve short exact sequences sectionwise, and exact module sheafification therefore makes $L$ exact. Here fixed-$A$ sheaves and $B$-module sheaves are identified by constant-scalar restriction, which leaves their underlying additive sheaves unchanged. A $B$-linear $h:LM\to F$ gives $t(m)=h_s(1\otimes m)$. Conversely $t:M\to F(s)$ gives a map from the constant presheaf by $m\mapsto t(m)|_U$, hence a unique map from its sheafification; extending $B$-linearly gives $b\otimes m\mapsto b\,t(m)|_U$. Restriction compatibility follows from $(t(m)|_U)|_W=t(m)|_W$. The composites are the identity on $m$ and on $1\otimes m$, hence on all local sections after sheafification. These formulas prove $L\dashv\Gamma$ and its naturality.

source.place: Tags 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules), 03EI (lemma-sheafification-exact), 093J (lemma-constant-exact); explicit adjunction from the sheafification universal property.

proof.text: The valuation-ring theorem gives that $R$ is a DVR with finite residue field, and the finite-quotient theorem applies to the chosen uniformizer and $n\ge1$, so $A$ is finite. Apply the finite-constant-sections theorem with $X=V=s$. The space $|s|$ has one point, so evaluation at that point identifies $C(|s|,A)$ with $A$. The stated normalization on constant-presheaf elements shows that its inverse is precisely $a\mapsto a\cdot1\in\Gamma B$. Exactness of $\Gamma$ on all $B$-module sheaves, and preservation of quasi-isomorphisms by termwise $\Gamma$, are the point-sections-exactness theorem.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.12, printed p. 30, applied to the final object Spec k; point-sections exactness as in Stacks Tags 0982 and 098H.

proof.text: Apply termwise-adjunction on homotopy categories and exact-functor derived factorization to $L,\Gamma$. The unit and counit are still the termwise maps just constructed: by clause (2) of the localization universal property they descend uniquely to natural transformations between the derived functors, and by clause (3) their naturality and triangle equalities remain equalities after localization. For $C\in D^b_c(s,A)$, sections finiteness gives $c=\Gamma C\in D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A)$. The finite branch of point-sections reconstruction applies: its exactness, constant-value ring identification and explicit adjunction hypotheses were verified in steps 1 and 2. It gives that the actual counit $e_C:Lc\to C$ is an isomorphism, natural in $C$. The triangle equality is $\Gamma(e_C)u_{\Gamma C}=1_{\Gamma C}$, so its unit is exactly the asserted $u_c$.

source.place: Second sentence: compute point internal Hom over coefficients; exact realization, reconstruction and arbitrary-target resolution model (old item steps 2 and 3).

proof.text: Work throughout on the small site skeleton fixed in the definition of $s_{\mathrm{proet}}$. K-flat resolution existence, also applied to the one-object site with ring $A$, supplies a flat-term K-flat representative $P\to c$. K-injective resolution existence on the small ringed site supplies $V\to J$, with no boundedness restriction on $V$. Since $\Gamma$ is right adjoint to the exact functor $L$, right-adjoint preservation of K-injectives gives that $\Gamma J$ is K-injective over $A$. Exactness of $\Gamma$ gives the quasi-isomorphism $\Gamma V\to\Gamma J$.

source.place: Tag 08BJ, lemma-adjoint-preserve-K-injectives; resolution-existence statements used on the fixed small site and the one-object module site.

proof.text:
Global Hom cochains identify degree $r$ of $\Gamma\mathcal Hom_B^\bullet(LP,J)$ with $\prod_i\operatorname{Hom}_B(LP^i,J^{i+r})$. Apply the degreewise adjunction of step 1 to every factor. The result is $\prod_i\operatorname{Hom}_A(P^i,\Gamma J^{i+r})$, and the maps are $q(h)(x)=h_s(1\otimes x)$ and $q^{-1}(t)(b\otimes x)=b\,t(x)|_U$. Products here are arbitrary sectionwise products; no finite-generation or boundedness of $P,J$ is used. In degree $r$, evaluation gives
$$q(dh)(x)=d_{\Gamma J}(q(h)(x))-(-1)^r q(h)(d_Px)=d(q(h))(x),$$
since $d_{LP}(1\otimes x)=1\otimes d_Px$. Thus these inverse degreewise maps are the claimed chain isomorphism $q_{P,J}$.

source.place: Hom-complex construction and global-cohomology-hom-complex; explicit degreewise adjunction calculation refining the point blueprint sentence.

proof.text: The derived-internal-Hom definition computes $R\mathcal Hom_B(Lc,V)$ by $\mathcal Hom_B^\bullet(LP,J)$, because $LP$ represents $Lc$ and $J$ is K-injective. Over the one-object ringed site the same definition computes $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(c,\Gamma V)$ by $\operatorname{Hom}_A^\bullet(P,\Gamma J)$, using step 4. Exact $\Gamma$ needs no resolution of the Hom complex: by exact-functor derived factorization, termwise $\Gamma$ of $\mathcal Hom_B^\bullet(LP,J)$ represents $\Gamma R\mathcal Hom_B(Lc,V)$. Therefore localizing the chain isomorphism of step 5 gives $q_{c,V}$ with the asserted direction. For different representatives the Hom-quasi-isomorphism lemma, on each of these two sites, supplies the comparison quasi-isomorphisms in the first variable and between K-injective representatives in the second. On the sheaf side exact $\Gamma$ preserves these maps as quasi-isomorphisms.

source.place: Tags 0A94 and 0A95, lemma-RHom-into-K-injective and lemma-RHom-well-defined; apply also on the one-object site for ordinary modules.

proof.text:
For chain maps $a:P'\to P$ and $b:J\to J'$, the formula in step 5 gives
$$q_{P',J'}(b\,h\,L(a))=(\Gamma b)\,q_{P,J}(h)\,a.$$
Indeed both sides send $x$ to $b_s(h_s(1\otimes a(x)))$. This proves commutation with every resolving comparison map in step 6. K-injective Hom-to-derived bijectivity represents any derived target morphism by a chain map between K-injective resolutions, uniquely up to homotopy; their changes are homotopy equivalences. In the source variable the derived category is localization at quasi-isomorphisms. The localization universal property therefore descends these commuting comparisons uniquely to the derived bifunctors. Naturality for an inverted quasi-isomorphism follows by inverting its commuting square, and then holds for every composite representing a derived morphism. This proves independence of $P,J$ and naturality of $q_{c,V}$ in both variables, not only for chain maps.

source.place: Tag 070I, lemma-K-injective; localization universal property and the explicit adjunct formula.

proof.text:
Precompose the first argument of internal Hom with the actual isomorphism $e_C:L\Gamma C\to C$ from step 3. Contravariance gives the isomorphism $R\mathcal Hom_B(C,V)\to R\mathcal Hom_B(Lc,V)$. Composing its sections with $q_{c,V}$ defines exactly $Q_{C,V}$ in the statement. For $f:C\to C'$ naturality of the counit reads $f e_C=e_{C'}L(\Gamma f)$; combining this equality with the naturality of $q$ proved in step 7 gives
$$R\operatorname{Hom}_A(\Gamma f,\Gamma V)Q_{C',V}=Q_{C,V}\,\Gamma R\mathcal Hom_B(f,V).$$
Covariance for $V\to V'$ follows from the same naturality of $q$ and of internal Hom. Both assertions apply to all derived morphisms by step 7, and the composite is independent of resolving representatives.
